# Parser conventions (`lib/src/parser/`)

## Token grammar

- A parser implements `WindParserInterface`: `canParse(String className)` and `parse(WindStyle styles, List<String>? classes, WindContext context)`. `canParse` is a cheap `startsWith` or a `static final RegExp`, and it sees the class after its last `:`, because `WindParser.resolveClasses` has already resolved the responsive, state, `dark:` and platform prefixes.
- Routing is first-match-wins in `_parserMap` order (`lib/src/parser/wind_parser.dart`). Register a more specific prefix before a more general one, and give a new parser its entry there, or it is never asked.
- `parse` returns `styles.copyWith(...)`, never null, and never mutates the input list.
- A colour-bearing parser (background, text, border, ring, shadow, svg fill and stroke) strips the `/N` opacity suffix with `parseColorOpacity` (`lib/src/utils/color_utils.dart`, which returns the record `({String colorPart, double? opacity})`) before matching the colour, then applies it with `applyOpacity`. Other parsers skip the step.
- Read the platform from `WindContext.platform`, never from `Platform.is*` or `defaultTargetPlatform`: the context's platform is part of the cache key, so a direct read would be cached under the wrong key.

## Last class in a family wins

`findAndGroupClasses` keeps duplicate classes on purpose (no `.toSet()`), so `top-8 top-4 top-8` must resolve to 8. Do not deduplicate. Inside a parser use one of two patterns:

- Walk `classes` in reverse and set each property only while it is still null (`??=`), as `padding_parser.dart` does. Prefer this one.
- Walk forward and overwrite on every match, as `border_parser.dart` does. Reset the competing properties explicitly, as a uniform width clearing the directional ones does there, or an earlier class survives a later one.

## Box decoration

`WindStyle.copyWith` must not fabricate an empty `BoxDecoration`: pass `decoration:` only when a class sets a real box property (colour, border, radius, shadow, gradient, image). Widgets wrap a box on `decoration != null`, so a fabricated one gives every padding-only or text-only style a needless wrapper.

## Short-circuit

`_parseAndCache` stops iterating parsers once `styles.isHidden` is true. That is the only built-in short-circuit; do not add another inside a parser, because a skipped parser silently drops its classes.
